feature: MTAP loss (homozygous 9p21 deletion, co-deleted with CDKN2A)
test_name: MTAP IHC (clone 2G4 or EPR6358) with loss defined as complete absence of cytoplasmic staining in tumor cells with retained internal control in stromal lymphocytes/endothelium
tissue_type: archival FFPE from the subtotal-resection specimen
rationale: The MTAPESTRY 101 phase 1 of AMG 193 (NCT05094336) showed that 4 of 6 patients enrolled on local CDKN2A deletion calls had intact MTAP on central IHC and progressed on therapy, which made central MTAP-null confirmation by an assay specified in the protocol a hard gate for every MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor program (AMG 193, MRTX1719, TNG462) and the MAT2A inhibitor IDE397. Tumor NGS copy-number alone is the wrong resolution for enrollment because the 9p21 region has a low signal-to-noise call rate and CDKN2A loss does not always extend through MTAP. Skipping IHC risks enrolling on a non-target and forfeiting the highest-yield molecular axis in this case.
turnaround_estimate: 5-7 business days once block is pulled
decision_gated: AMG 193 (MTAPESTRY 101 / NCT05094336) and other MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor and MAT2A inhibitor trial enrollment in MTAP-null GBM.

providers.name: NeoGenomics Laboratories
providers.notes: High-volume CAP-accredited IHC lab; runs MTAP routinely on the same panel many PRMT5 trials use for central confirmation, so the result is generally accepted by trial central labs without a re-stain. Fastest commercial turnaround for the same block already in pathology.

providers.name: Foundation Medicine
providers.notes: FoundationOne CDx is the FDA-cleared NGS call; the linked MTAP IHC service is being co-developed with Bristol Myers Squibb as the companion diagnostic across MTAP-deleted indications. Useful when the same vendor reads NGS and IHC together.

providers.name: Caris Life Sciences
providers.notes: Bundles MTAP IHC with the MI Profile NGS report; reasonable when comprehensive molecular profile is being ordered together.

providers.name: Memorial Sloan Kettering Diagnostic Molecular Pathology
providers.notes: Academic alternative for MSK-network patients; MSK-IMPACT is well-validated for 9p21 copy-number calling and pathology will run MTAP IHC on consult.

notes: If the existing NGS report names the assay used for the MTAP copy-number call and the trial central lab accepts that assay, the IHC may move to a confirmation-on-arrival step at the trial site rather than a pre-screen. When in doubt, send IHC first; it is cheap and the consequence of a false positive enrollment is large.

test_name: MGMT promoter methylation by pyrosequencing (4-5 CpG sites in exon 1, cutoff approximately 8-10% average methylation) with reflex to methylation-specific PCR if pyrosequencing fails
tissue_type: archival FFPE from the subtotal-resection specimen
rationale: MGMT promoter methylation is the strongest predictor of temozolomide benefit in IDH-wildtype GBM; methylated tumors derive a 7-8 month median-survival advantage on Stupp, unmethylated tumors derive limited TMZ benefit and become priority candidates for TMZ-sparing or TMZ-alternative front-line trials. Pyrosequencing is the most prognostic of the available methods; the Reifenberger comparison found pyrosequencing best separated patients who benefited from temozolomide, with the 8-10% CpG-average threshold defining the cutoff. The case has no MGMT call recorded; without it the adjuvant TMZ commitment is being made blind and the patient cannot be triaged into an MGMT-stratified trial.
decision_gated: Adjuvant temozolomide commitment (Stupp); triage into MGMT-stratified front-line trials including TMZ-sparing arms for unmethylated tumors.

providers.name: Labcorp Oncology
providers.notes: Holds the exclusive US license from OncoMethylome for the quantitative MSP method validated against the EORTC 26981/22981 cohort; the most widely accepted commercial MGMT call and the one most neuro-oncology trial protocols recognize. Fastest national turnaround.

providers.name: NeoGenomics Laboratories
providers.notes: Bisulfite + real-time PCR with a quantitative CpG methylation readout; reasonable alternative when Labcorp turnaround is constrained.

providers.name: Mayo Clinic Laboratories
providers.notes: Pyrosequencing-based call (the method that best separated TMZ benefit in the Quillien comparison); the most defensible quantitative result when the case sits near the 8-10% cutoff.

providers.name: University of Michigan MLabs
providers.address: 1500 East Medical Center Drive, Ann Arbor, MI 48109

notes: The intake explicitly flags MGMT as the highest-priority diagnostic gap. Run it before the adjuvant TMZ commitment is finalized; unmethylated patients are the population for whom TMZ-sparing trials are most worth chasing.

test_name: EGFR amplification by FISH or NGS copy-number plus EGFRvIII-specific testing by RT-PCR or RNA-based NGS fusion panel; report both amplification ratio and vIII status separately
tissue_type: archival FFPE from the subtotal-resection specimen
rationale: EGFR amplification is present in roughly 40-50% of IDH-wildtype GBM (INTELLANCE screening cohort) and EGFRvIII appears in approximately 20-30% of EGFR-amplified tumors; vIII status is the binary gate for EGFRvIII-directed CAR-T (including E-SYNC, tandem EGFRvIII/IL-13Ra2 CAR-T, and oncolytic-virus-delivered bispecific platforms). Pan-EGFR amplification without vIII opens a separate set of EGFR ADC and bispecific protocols. The current report has neither call. Without resolution the patient is invisible to the most active GBM cellular-therapy trial families.
decision_gated: EGFRvIII-directed CAR-T and bispecific trial enrollment (E-SYNC, tandem EGFRvIII/IL-13Ra2, oncolytic-virus platforms); EGFR-amplification ADC and bispecific protocols.

providers.name: Foundation Medicine
providers.notes: Single comprehensive report covers EGFR copy-number, vIII as a sequence-level call when the deletion is captured by the panel, plus the other gating biomarkers in this case (CDKN2A, MTAP context, TERT promoter, BRAF, MMR). Most efficient bundle when several biomarker rows can be answered from one block.

providers.name: NeoGenomics Laboratories
providers.notes: Carries a dedicated EGFRvIII RT-PCR assay; the standalone vIII call is often what GBM cellular-therapy trial central labs ask for as a screening result.

providers.name: Tempus Labs
providers.notes: Comprehensive DNA + RNA bundle; RNA-seq picks up EGFRvIII reliably when the breakpoint is covered.

providers.name: Memorial Sloan Kettering Diagnostic Molecular Pathology

notes: Many GBM trials require both an amplification ratio (FISH ≥2.0 or copy-number ≥5) and a separately-reported vIII call; ensure both are documented in the path report rather than inferred from a generic NGS panel.

test_name: Comprehensive tumor NGS panel covering TERT promoter, chromosome 7 / chromosome 10 copy-number, BRAF V600E, NTRK1/2/3 fusions, MMR genes (MLH1/MSH2/MSH6/PMS2), TMB, MSI, plus IDH1/2, ATRX, EGFR, PTEN, NF1, PDGFRA, MET (FoundationOne CDx, MSK-IMPACT, Tempus xT, or Caris MI Cancer Seek)
tissue_type: archival FFPE from the subtotal-resection specimen
rationale: Six high-priority biomarkers (TERT promoter, +7/-10, BRAF V600E, NTRK fusions, MMR status, comprehensive copy-number) are unresolved and each opens a different therapeutic branch: BRAF V600E gates the tumor-agnostic dabrafenib + trametinib label (ROAR phase 2 high-grade glioma cohort, ORR 33%), NTRK fusions gate larotrectinib/entrectinib, MMR loss or MSI-high gates tumor-agnostic pembrolizumab, and TERT/+7/-10 confirm molecular GBM classification under cIMPACT-NOW Update 3. Running these as a single comprehensive panel is far more efficient than serial single-gene tests, and the same panel resolves the EGFR amplification and vIII context, CDKN2A homozygous-loss call, and a TMB number for the ICI rationale. Skipping forfeits four tumor-agnostic therapeutic options and weakens the molecular GBM diagnosis.
tissue_required_estimate: 1 FFPE block or 10-20 unstained slides; archival acceptable
decision_gated: Dabrafenib + trametinib (BRAF V600E), larotrectinib / entrectinib (NTRK fusion), tumor-agnostic pembrolizumab (TMB-H or MSI-H / dMMR), and confirmatory molecular-GBM classification.

providers.name: Foundation Medicine
providers.notes: FDA-approved companion diagnostic for the tumor-agnostic pembrolizumab TMB indication and for the BRAF V600E label; covers TERT promoter, MMR genes, NTRK fusions (DNA-level), EGFR, CDKN2A, and MTAP on one report. The most defensible single bundle for this case.

providers.name: Memorial Sloan Kettering Diagnostic Molecular Pathology
providers.notes: Academic-network alternative; ~1.5 Mb panel size well-validated for TMB and comprehensive CN calling. Restricted to MSK referrals.

providers.name: Tempus Labs
providers.notes: DNA + RNA combination is the strongest assay for NTRK-fusion detection in CNS tumors, where DNA-only panels can miss intron-deep breakpoints.

providers.name: Caris Life Sciences
providers.notes: Whole-transcriptome RNA arm catches the same NTRK-fusion class as Tempus xR.

notes: One comprehensive NGS bundle resolves multiple rows in this file (EGFR amplification, CDKN2A copy-number context, MTAP context, TERT, +7/-10, BRAF, NTRK, MMR, TMB, MSI). Run it as a single send-out and the downstream rows collapse to chart-review confirmations.

test_name: RB1 status (NGS variant call plus RB protein IHC with clone G3-245) to confirm intact RB pathway downstream of CDK4/6
tissue_type: archival FFPE from the subtotal-resection specimen
rationale: CDK4/6 inhibitors only work when RB is intact; RB1 loss or mutation drives primary resistance because the kinase substrate that CDK4/6 phosphorylates is gone. The abemaciclib recurrent-GBM phase 2 (NCT02981940) explicitly required CDKN2A/B loss with intact RB as the eligibility pair. Tumor NGS that reports RB1 wild-type at the DNA level still misses cases where RB protein is lost post-transcriptionally, so a quick IHC corroboration locks the pathway integrity. Without it the CDK4/6 inhibitor rationale is incomplete.
turnaround_estimate: 5-7 business days for IHC; same panel as the comprehensive NGS for the variant call
tissue_required_estimate: 1 unstained slide; can share the p16/MTAP block
decision_gated: Abemaciclib (CNS-penetrant) and other CDK4/6 inhibitor eligibility in recurrent/progressive GBM with CDKN2A loss; protocols explicitly require intact RB.

providers.name: NeoGenomics Laboratories
providers.notes: Bundle on the same IHC requisition as MTAP and p16; one pathology hand-off resolves the entire 9p21/RB-pathway-integrity question.

providers.name: Memorial Sloan Kettering Pathology Consultation Service

notes: If the comprehensive NGS panel reports RB1 as wild-type and the path report already documents intact RB on a related stain, this row collapses to a chart-review pass. Otherwise add the IHC to the 9p21 IHC bundle.

test_name: p16/INK4a IHC (clone E6H4 or JC8) with homozygous-loss pattern defined as complete absence of nuclear and cytoplasmic staining in tumor cells with retained internal control
tissue_type: archival FFPE from the subtotal-resection specimen
rationale: p16 IHC loss correlates with CDKN2A homozygous deletion at high negative predictive value, but the orthogonal protein-level call is what most CDK4/6 inhibitor protocols and tumor boards expect when the rationale rests on a single NGS copy-number signal. The IHC also catches the cases where CDKN2A is functionally silenced by promoter methylation without a DNA-level deletion, which a copy-number-only assay misses. Skipping the IHC leaves the abemaciclib / palbociclib / ribociclib rationale resting on a single panel call and weakens the case for CDK4/6 inhibitor trial enrollment.
decision_gated: CDK4/6 inhibitor (abemaciclib favored for CNS penetration) trial enrollment; complements the CDKN2A NGS call rather than gating it.

providers.name: NeoGenomics Laboratories
providers.notes: Routine commercial IHC with E6H4 clone; bundle on the same requisition as the MTAP IHC so a single block handoff covers both 9p21 protein readouts.

providers.name: Memorial Sloan Kettering Pathology Consultation Service

notes: p16 IHC and MTAP IHC are best ordered together as a 9p21 protein-readout pair; one block, two stains, one report.

test_name: Whole-genome DNA methylation profiling with the Heidelberg/DKFZ CNS tumor classifier (Illumina EPIC array, v12.8 or later), reporting methylation class, subclass score, and MGMT promoter methylation status from the same array
tissue_type: archival FFPE from the subtotal-resection specimen
rationale: The Heidelberg classifier resolves IDH-wildtype GBM into RTK I (pediatric-type), RTK II (the most common adult subtype, enriched for 9p21/CDKN2A homozygous loss and EGFR amplification), and mesenchymal subclasses; this case sits in the genomic territory of RTK II and the classifier confirms it. cIMPACT-NOW Update 9 (2025) now recommends methylation profiling for high-grade glioma cases with diagnostic ambiguity, and the classifier impacted the final diagnosis in 46.7% of high-confidence cases in the multicentric validation. The same array also returns an MGMT call from a different probe set, so it doubles as orthogonal MGMT validation. The Heidelberg Epignostix CPT code took effect in CMS reimbursement in January, which makes the test accessible through US clinical labs.
decision_gated: Subtype refinement (RTK I vs RTK II vs mesenchymal) for trial enrollment prioritization; orthogonal MGMT methylation call from the same array.

providers.name: Heidelberg Epignostix GmbH
providers.notes: The original DKFZ classifier; the most-cited reference for CNS tumor methylation classification. Software-as-a-service model integrated into US clinical labs that run the EPIC array.

providers.name: NeoGenomics Laboratories
providers.notes: US-based commercial lab that runs the Illumina EPIC array and submits to the Heidelberg classifier under the new CPT code; fastest domestic turnaround for the same workflow.

providers.name: Johns Hopkins Molecular Pathology
providers.notes: Academic-center alternative; well-validated against the Heidelberg cohort.

providers.name: Memorial Sloan Kettering Diagnostic Molecular Pathology

notes: If the comprehensive NGS panel and MGMT pyrosequencing are already covering the diagnostic and predictive bases, the methylation classifier is most valuable when the histology is ambiguous, when subclass-targeted trial enrollment is on the table, or as orthogonal MGMT validation when the pyrosequencing result sits at the borderline.

test_name: CDK4 and CCND1/2/3 amplification status on the comprehensive NGS panel (FoundationOne CDx, MSK-IMPACT, or Tempus xT) with copy-number thresholds reported
tissue_type: archival FFPE; same block as the comprehensive NGS
rationale: CDK4 amplification or CCND1/2/3 amplification co-occurring with CDKN2A loss creates a stronger pharmacodynamic substrate for CDK4/6 inhibition than CDKN2A loss alone, and several CDK4/6 inhibitor protocols stratify or prioritize patients with the compound CDK4 amp / CDKN2A loss genotype. The call comes off the same comprehensive NGS panel that resolves EGFR and the other rows, so the marginal cost is zero. Refines the CDK4/6 inhibitor rationale and trial prioritization but does not gate enrollment in CDKN2A-only protocols.
turnaround_estimate: same as the comprehensive NGS turnaround (2-4 weeks)
tissue_required_estimate: shared with the comprehensive NGS block
decision_gated: CDK4/6 inhibitor trial prioritization for the compound CDKN2A-loss + CDK4-amp genotype; complements CDKN2A loss rather than gating CDK4/6 inhibitor eligibility on its own.

providers.name: Foundation Medicine
providers.notes: Reports CDK4, CCND1, CCND2, CCND3 copy-number on the same FoundationOne CDx report as CDKN2A and MTAP; the call collapses to a chart-review pass once the comprehensive panel returns.

providers.name: Memorial Sloan Kettering Diagnostic Molecular Pathology

notes: No new send-out required; this row is a documentation check on the comprehensive-NGS report. If neither CDK4 nor CCND is amplified, the CDK4/6 inhibitor rationale still holds on CDKN2A loss alone but the case is weaker.

feature: MTAP loss (homozygous 9p21 deletion, co-deleted with CDKN2A)
test_name: Plasma SDMA (symmetric dimethylarginine) baseline by LC-MS/MS, with paired on-treatment draw at cycle 2 day 1 if a PRMT5 inhibitor trial is started
tissue_type: 5-10 mL EDTA plasma; no tumor required
rationale: SDMA is the most proximal pharmacodynamic readout of PRMT5 inhibition, and the BMS-986504 phase 1 reported a 56% median plasma SDMA reduction from baseline to cycle 2 day 1 in MTAP-deleted responders, with the top dose tiers reaching 60%. A baseline draw before starting any PRMT5 inhibitor gives the team a reference for on-treatment target engagement; without it the on-treatment number is uninterpretable. Most PRMT5 inhibitor trials already collect this on protocol, so the row often becomes a confirmation that the trial central lab is doing the draw rather than a separate send-out.
decision_gated: On-treatment PRMT5-inhibitor target-engagement monitoring; informs whether to push dose or switch agents at first scan if SDMA reduction is inadequate.

providers.name: Trial central laboratory (per protocol)
providers.notes: The MTAPESTRY 101 protocol and most other MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor protocols collect plasma SDMA on study; the trial central lab is the default provider. If a separate baseline is needed before trial enrollment, route through the academic medical center's clinical research laboratory.

providers.name: ARUP Laboratories
providers.address: 500 Chipeta Way, Salt Lake City, UT 84108
providers.notes: Offers SDMA on a CLIA-validated LC-MS/MS workflow; useful when a pre-enrollment baseline is needed outside the trial central lab.

notes: Defer unless the patient is being enrolled on a PRMT5 inhibitor trial that does not already collect SDMA, or unless the team wants an early target-engagement readout to decide whether to push dose.

test_name: Germline panel covering CDKN2A (familial melanoma-astrocytoma syndrome), MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2 (Lynch / CMMRD), TP53 (Li-Fraumeni), NF1, and the DNA-repair genes triggered by any tumor-side MMR loss
tissue_type: 5-10 mL EDTA whole blood or saliva kit
rationale: Germline CDKN2A pathogenic variants drive the familial atypical multiple-mole melanoma syndrome (FAMMM), which carries elevated melanoma and pancreatic cancer risk and a small but recognized GBM risk; the homozygous-loss tumor finding is the kind of result that warrants asking whether one of the hits is germline. If the tumor-side MMR / MSI panel returns dMMR or MSI-H, the same germline panel triggers the Lynch / CMMRD workup that informs first-degree-relative cascade testing. The 66-year-old age makes a high-penetrance germline syndrome less likely but does not exclude it; the test is cheap relative to the implications.
tissue_required_estimate: 5-10 mL EDTA whole blood or saliva kit
decision_gated: Cascade testing of first-degree relatives if a high-penetrance germline variant is identified; reframes surveillance recommendations for the patient.

providers.name: Labcorp Genetics (formerly Invitae)
providers.notes: Broadest US hereditary-cancer panel with strong payer acceptance and a financial-assistance program that meaningfully reduces patient out-of-pocket. Covers CDKN2A, the Lynch genes, TP53, NF1, and the DNA-repair gene set in a single send-out.

providers.name: Myriad Genetics
providers.address: 320 Wakara Way, Salt Lake City, UT 84108

notes: Pair with genetic counseling. If the tumor-side MMR or MSI signal returns abnormal on the comprehensive NGS, escalate this row to high priority.

feature: MTAP loss (homozygous 9p21 deletion, co-deleted with CDKN2A)
test_name: MAT2A protein expression by IHC on archival FFPE (research-grade antibody; report nuclear and cytoplasmic intensity)
tissue_type: archival FFPE; can share the MTAP block
rationale: MAT2A is the upstream enzyme that supplies S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) to PRMT5; in MTAP-null tumors, MTA accumulation makes PRMT5 partially dependent on MAT2A flux, which is the synthetic-lethal rationale for MAT2A inhibitors (IDE397, AG-270). Protein-level corroboration is not required for IDE397 enrollment, which gates on MTAP-null status alone, but a baseline MAT2A protein signal helps interpret why a given patient responds or fails. The assay is research-grade and most useful as a translational add-on rather than a clinical decision step.
decision_gated: Translational characterization of MAT2A-inhibitor target context (IDE397, AG-270); does not gate enrollment, which runs off MTAP-null status.

providers.name: Memorial Sloan Kettering Pathology Consultation Service
providers.notes: Academic pathology consult is the most realistic route for a research-grade MAT2A stain; most commercial labs do not run it as a menu item.

notes: Strictly optional; consider only if a MAT2A inhibitor trial is being seriously pursued and the trial team requests it. The MTAP IHC + comprehensive NGS bundle already covers the clinical decision.
